text:
maya: FYI customer ACME (via support@acme.com) reporting repeated API 5xx / timeouts for hosted inference since ~08:40 UTC. They say errors started after a traffic spike. stack traces show upstream cache errors. Can someone triage?

jordan: Customer says ~30% of requests returning 502/gateway timeouts, high tail latency. They included sample request ids: req_9a2f, req_b3c1, req_d7e0. Happening across models (gpt-like and embeddings).

oncall-bot: Incident alert: redis-prefix-cache-us-east elevated errors > 5% for 10m.

maya: Attached logs from customer's session: 
```
2026-03-15T08:42:11Z ERR cache/prefix: timeout getting prefix KV for key="session:acme:prefix:abcd" err="i/o timeout"
2026-03-15T08:42:12Z WARN runtime: falling back to direct compute for request=req_9a2f
2026-03-15T08:42:12Z ERR gateway: upstream 502 from cache service
```

eli: I'm on it. Initial look at host metrics for redis-prefix-cache-us-east: p99 latency spiked to 2.3s, connection churn high, role-change events around 08:38. Could be a failover thrash on one of the nodes.

samir: If the prefix/KV cache is synchronous in the request path, timeouts will bubble up as 5xx. We have circuit-breaker logic, but threshold may be too permissive for this workload.

grace: Checking infra: AWS replaced a failed instance in the cluster at 08:37 and automated failover started. I'm seeing a backlog of replication syncs after the OOM-triggered eviction.

maya: Customer asked for quick mitigation — they can't degrade. Any short-term workaround we can offer them?

samir: Two quick mitigations: 1) Flip customer route to bypass prefix caching (toggle in route config) so requests don't block on Redis. 2) Enable local in-memory LRU cache as a temporary fallback for prefix hits. Both will increase token cost but restore availability.

eli: I can push a canary for bypass in their tenant config. Need a support approval note and confirmation from infra.

grace: Infra will increase redis connections and patch the node, but failover replication might take 10-15m. Recommend bypass first.

maya: I'll propose bypass + postmortem. Jordan, can you get ACME approval for temporary bypass and tell them expected impact?

jordan: Reached out, they approved bypass for emergency. Concerned about higher cost but prefer uptime.

samir: Steps I'm going to run now (will paste exact commands):
```
# show current route config for tenant
curl -H "Authorization: Bearer $ADMIN_TOKEN" https://console.api.redwood.ai/v1/routes/acme -s | jq .cache
# set prefix_cache.enabled = false
curl -X PATCH -H "Authorization: Bearer $ADMIN_TOKEN" -d '{"cache":{"prefix_cache":false}}' https://console.api.redwood.ai/v1/routes/acme
```

eli: Before applying, capture baseline metrics: cache error rate, p99 latency, request success rate.

maya: Baseline captured. Proceed with change when ready.

samir: Applied change at 08:50 UTC. Rolling prop change to 2% of traffic -> 20% -> 100% with quick checks in between.

oncall-bot: Deployment: route-config-update by samir applied to tenant acme at 1778000500.

eli: After bypass: error rates for that tenant dropped to <0.5% within 60s. Global cache error rate still elevated because other tenants hit same cluster.

grace: Redis cluster stabilized after patch/restart at ~08:54; replication lag cleared. We're still seeing a few slow nodes but overall healthy.

maya: Customer confirmed service restored, they reported normal success rates at 08:55.

jordan: Customer asks for root cause and what we will do to prevent recurrence. They also want guidance on best practices for critical workloads.

samir: Root cause summary (for postmortem):
- Primary: Redis node OOM triggered eviction/latency under traffic spike.
- Secondary: AWS host replacement led to role-change/failover thrash increasing p99 latency and connection churn.
- System design issue: Synchronous prefix/KV cache calls in the hot path amplified effect, and circuit-breaker thresholds were too high.

samir: Short-term fixes already applied: tenant bypass for prefix cache, patched the unhealthy node, increased fallback thresholds.

samir: Medium-term actions proposed:
- Move prefix cache calls to async-safe path with timeout < 200ms and immediate fallback to compute path.
- Add adaptive circuit breaker which lowers concurrency to cache service during high error rates.
- Harden redis cluster autoscaling and tune maxmemory-policy to avoid OOM under bursts.
- Provide customer-facing runbook: recommended route config toggles and impact.

grace: Infra action items: investigate kernel logs and memory pressure patterns, pin redis version and test failover behavior under load, add more aggressive HPA for cache fleet in us-east.

eli: Eng-runtime action items: implement timeout cutoffs + async path in next sprint and backport a hotfix for sync codepaths.

maya: Support action items: send immediate incident note to ACME with timeline and mitigations. Offer 10% credit for downtime window per SLA policy.

jordan: ACME accepted the explanation and temporary credit. Wants weekly updates until the medium-term fixes land.

samir: I'll open a follow-up PR with the canary config and circuit-breaker thresholds. Also adding a smoke test that emulates prefix cache timeouts to catch regressions.

maya: Thanks everyone. Recording notes for postmortem. Will file incident ticket and link this thread.

oncall-bot: Ticket created: INC-2026-0423-redis-prefix-cache-thrash. Assigned: grace, samir, eli.

eli: If anyone wants the raw telemetry I pulled (histograms, traces, spans), DM me and I'll share the S3 bundle.

maya: Closing thread for now. If any new customer regressions reported, re-open or ping oncall. :white_check_mark:
